warnings: *** THE BRANCH-SIZE TABLE ('ขนาดท่อย่อยที่ต่อเข้าสุขภัณฑ์') IS THE MOST REUSABLE DATA ON THIS SHEET *** -- eight fixture types against four services (CW / S / V / W), which is what actually determines the small-bore pipe quantities. It is recorded as one branch_pipe_spec element per fixture rather than as free text.

*** WATCH THE '1' SUFFIX -- IT MEANS SOMETHING DIFFERENT HERE THAN IN THE ARCHITECTURAL SET. *** In this table WC1 is a FLUSH-VALVE water closet (FV.) as against WC, the cistern type (FT.), and the difference is real: WC1 needs a ø1" cold-water branch where WC needs only ø3/4". On A-29 the same style of suffix marks a different BASIN (LAV1 = counter-inset vs LAV = wall-hung). Same notation, unrelated meanings.

THE HOUSE USES THE CISTERN TYPE. A-29 schedules 'โถส้วมนั่งราบแบบหม้อน้ำซักโครก' -- a flush-tank WC -- so the WC row (ø3/4" CW) applies, not the WC1 row. The WC1 row is a standard table entry that is not used in this house.

TWO TABLE ROWS ARE FOR FIXTURES THIS HOUSE DOES NOT HAVE: UR. (urinal) and, arguably, WC1. The table is a standard office table carried onto the sheet, so its presence is not evidence that the fixture exists. Cross-check against A-29 before pricing.

ONLY THE ISOMETRICS SHOW THE ø1 1/2" FIXTURE VENTS. The floor plans SN-04/SN-05 tag only ø2"V, so a take-off done from the plans alone will miss the smaller vent branches that the table and these isometrics both call for.
The upper isometric tags no ø4"S even though the plan directly above it does -- an omission in the isometric, not a design difference.
Both bathroom plans match the architectural room dimensions exactly (2.30 x 3.40 for WC1, 2.40 x 2.90 for WC2), so sanitary and architecture agree on the rooms.
